values.note: County ordinance: overnight stays limited to 7 days in a 31-day period and 21 days in any 12 months; RVs and trailers must be registered and roadworthy. The ordinance describes no reservation or permit, so camping is on arrival.

booking.source: https://bleckley.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/0035_001.pdf (James Dykes Memorial Park Camping Ordinance, adopted 2022-10-20: 'Overnight stays at the park are limited to 7 days in a 31-day period'; 'Overnight stays in excess of 21 days in any continuous 12-month period is prohibited'; no reservation or permit provision), read 2026-10-30

facilities.source: https://bleckley.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/0035_001.pdf ('Sewage must be disposed of at an off-site facility. Campers shall retain copies of dump receipts'), read 2026-10-30

summary: Bleckley County's camping ordinance (the only county page) confirms RV/trailer camping at the landing, 7 nights in 31 days (plus a 21-nights-a-year cap) and off-site sewage disposal (dump false). It states no fee, no reservation and no facilities; free/FCFS, no water or toilets stay as earlier prose. Pin is on the gravel landing beside the ramp.
flags: Missing phone: no campground number is published; the county's own page gives Bleckley County, 112 N 2nd Street, Cochran, 478-934-3200 (https://bleckley.org/).
Fees: the county ordinance says nothing about a fee; the stored free (0/0) comes from earlier note prose and no county page confirms or contradicts it.

Inclusion judgement: camping is a county-designated use of a boat-landing park (ordinance: 'a park designed for recreation, relaxation, fishing, and camping'; it refers to 'camp sites'), not an incidental parking-lot allowance, but there are no marked sites, water, toilets or dump - the open gravel landing beside the ramp is roughly 0.5 ha on imagery.
